articles.headline: Friday Five — November 6, 2026 | Red Hat

body.text: Key Takeaway

The default Prometheus web UI is now exposed externally unless you turn it off [FACT:9758cdfeefb7a98c677667a0c21a15d4]. Remote‑write no longer publishes a public /write endpoint, and a new receiver‑count metric tells you how many remote‑write receivers are active [FACT:906acc5cdc17fd57cde504ffb1bfb8e2][FACT:d63496a66ff126f929f6f6452eab852d]. Exemplars missing timestamps are rejected, protecting the TSDB from silent corruption [FACT:511dcde2f206553b94580125e5f2cb4d]. The API now lets you override the max‑samples limit per query, giving finer‑grained control over query load [FACT:2dd2d847f45a5fec358e4c0a448d81a2].

Subqueries return the full set of samples instead of being capped, smoothing out gaps in Grafana panels [FACT:3a01c413e4b3817b0365bd962d93c14d]. The agent can write its own metadata WAL, improving crash recovery [FACT:2b461d52aa442a00bf5172dee091e8d6]. Finally, a new PromQL ‘smoothed’ operator produces anchored vectors for low‑noise trend lines [FACT:589ae68071cb148de60d335d90f8fa34].
Why This Matters

External UI exposure forces you to tighten network policies or add authentication, otherwise the dashboard is reachable from anywhere [FACT:9758cdfeefb7a98c677667a0c21a15d4]. Disabling the public remote‑write endpoint shrinks your attack surface, while the receiver‑count metric gives an instant health check on write pipelines [FACT:906acc5cdc17fd57cde504ffb1bfb8e2][FACT:d63496a66ff126f929f6f6452eab852d]. Rejecting malformed exemplars prevents corrupt data from inflating storage costs and spamming alerts [FACT:511dcde2f206553b94580125e5f2cb4d]. Overriding max‑samples per query lets bursty workloads run without raising the global limit, keeping the TSDB from choking under load [FACT:2dd2d847f45a5fec358e4c0a448d81a2].

Richer subquery results eliminate missing points that previously required manual interpolation in dashboards [FACT:3a01c413e4b3817b0365bd962d93c14d]. Metadata WAL on the agent means a node crash no longer loses recent scrape metadata, shortening recovery times [FACT:2b461d52aa442a00bf5172dee091e8d6]. The smoothed operator gives built‑in trend lines, reducing the need for external processing pipelines [FACT:589ae68071cb148de60d335d90f8fa34].
What Happened

The Prometheus configuration now defaults the web UI to external exposure [FACT:9758cdfeefb7a98c677667a0c21a15d4]. Remote‑write stopped exposing the /write endpoint and added a receiver‑count metric for pipeline visibility [FACT:906acc5cdc17fd57cde504ffb1bfb8e2][FACT:d63496a66ff126f929f6f6452eab852d]. TSDB logic was tightened to reject exemplar samples without timestamps [FACT:511dcde2f206553b94580125e5f2cb4d]. The query API gained a flag to override the max‑samples limit on a per‑query basis [FACT:2dd2d847f45a5fec358e4c0a448d81a2].

Subquery handling now returns all samples, improving time‑series continuity [FACT:3a01c413e4b3817b0365bd962d93c14d]. The agent added support for a metadata write‑ahead log, enhancing crash recovery [FACT:2b461d52aa442a00bf5172dee091e8d6]. A new PromQL smoothed function was introduced to generate anchored vectors for low‑noise analysis [FACT:589ae68071cb148de60d335d90f8fa34].
Builder View

If you run Prometheus in a Kubernetes pod, check the web.external‑enabled flag and disable it if you don’t need the UI exposed [FACT:9758cdfeefb7a98c677667a0c21a15d4]. Remove any reliance on the now‑removed /write endpoint and start monitoring the receiver‑count metric to spot stalled remote‑write pipelines [FACT:906acc5cdc17fd57cde504ffb1bfb8e2][FACT:d63496a66ff126f929f6f6452eab852d]. Audit your exporters for timestamps; missing ones will be dropped rather than silently stored [FACT:511dcde2f206553b94580125e5f2cb4d]. Use the –query.max‑samples‑override flag on heavy queries instead of raising the global limit [FACT:2dd2d847f45a5fec358e4c0a448d81a2].

Leverage the expanded subquery sample range to clean up Grafana dashboards without extra interpolation logic [FACT:3a01c413e4b3817b0365bd962d93c14d]. Enable the agent’s metadata WAL by setting agent.metadata‑wal=true in the config map to improve crash resilience [FACT:2b461d52aa442a00bf5172dee091e8d6]. Adopt the smoothed PromQL operator in alert rules to get stable trend alerts without external preprocessing [FACT:589ae68071cb148de60d335d90f8fa34].
Open Questions

The release notes introduce the receiver‑count metric [FACT:d63496a66ff126f929f6f6452eab852d] but do not provide baseline performance numbers, so clusters should benchmark its impact. The metadata WAL feature [FACT:2b461d52aa442a00bf5172dee091e8d6] promises quicker recovery after crashes, but real‑world durability benefits will become clear only after failure scenarios are exercised.
Ardur Take

Red Hat’s Friday Five flags eight concrete Prometheus tweaks that tighten security, improve query fidelity, and add useful observability knobs. Teams running Kubernetes should verify they’re on the latest release, audit the external UI exposure, enable the new receiver‑count metric, and adopt the metadata WAL and smoothed operator where appropriate [FACT:9758cdfeefb7a98c677667a0c21a15d4][FACT:906acc5cdc17fd57cde504ffb1bfb8e2][FACT:d63496a66ff126f929f6f6452eab852d][FACT:511dcde2f206553b94580125e5f2cb4d][FACT:2dd2d847f45a5fec358e4c0a448d81a2][FACT:3a01c413e4b3817b0365bd962d93c14d][FACT:2b461d52aa442a00bf5172dee091e8d6][FACT:589ae68071cb148de60d335d90f8fa34].

articles.headline: kpt 1.0.0 released — Porch integration lands, verification added
articles.dek: CNCF announced kpt v1.0.0 on Nov 5 2026, bringing Porch orchestration and built‑in KRM verification.

body.text: Key Takeaway

Version 1.0.0 of kpt ships with a built‑in Porch framework for package orchestration and a new KRM verification step, while staying a lightweight configuration tool [FACT:ada07bfd164bc5ff439a9b57bd421d17][FACT:36a6a6d35d857ab77d3885ab5ccd9510][FACT:6a489c26315c7fc4dae190035fb70c91].
Why This Matters

The addition of Porch means you can run a single kpt command to pull, render, and apply a set of packages, cutting the glue code you usually write for Helm or custom scripts [FACT:36a6a6d35d857ab77d3885ab5ccd9510]. The verification hook checks each KRM against the schema before it reaches the API server, catching typos early and reducing rollback pain [FACT:6a489c26315c7fc4dae190035fb70c91].
What Happened

CNCF’s blog confirmed that the kpt community released version 1.0.0 on 5 Nov 2026, marking the first major milestone after a year of stabilising the Porch package [FACT:e5e7071f6c482672a73f71ebba1f7b14][FACT:0aa49ab8ea176ca9d74f5a80a8c81c68].
Builder View

For builders, the practical impact is twofold: you can replace custom CI steps that stitch together kpt and Helm with a single Porch‑enabled kpt command [FACT:36a6a6d35d857ab77d3885ab5ccd9510][FACT:0aa49ab8ea176ca9d74f5a80a8c81c68], and you gain a built‑in safety net that verifies every KRM before it hits the API server [FACT:6a489c26315c7fc4dae190035fb70c91].
Open Questions
The kpt project meets weekly on Wednesdays, so you can follow the minutes for any deprecation notices that might affect your pipelines [FACT:0dbad7a6fec2e04290492dd73aef9226].
Ardur Take

With a single source confirming the release and the added Porch integration, confidence in the core changes is high; however, without independent performance data, we rate the operational impact as medium until community reports surface [FACT:e5e7071f6c482672a73f71ebba1f7b14].
